questions.question_text: Controlling is the management function of:
options: Measuring actual performance against standards and taking corrective action
questions.explanation: It ensures that plans are achieved.

options: The measurement and correction of the performance of subordinates to ensure that enterprise objectives and plans are accomplished
questions.explanation: It includes both measurement and correction.

options: Verifying whether everything occurs in conformity with the plan adopted, instructions issued and principles established
questions.explanation: Its aim is to point out weaknesses and errors to rectify them.

questions.question_text: A feature of controlling is that it:
options: Is goal-oriented, pervasive, continuous and both forward and backward-looking
questions.explanation: It also involves comparison and correction.

questions.question_text: Controlling is a pervasive function because it:
options: Is a function of one department
Is needed at all levels and in all departments
Is done by top managers only

questions.question_text: Controlling is a continuous function because:
options: Performance is monitored on an ongoing basis

questions.question_text: Controlling is both forward and backward-looking because:
options: It looks only at the future
It looks only at the past
It learns from past deviations to improve future plans
Accomplishing goals, improving efficiency and ensuring order and discipline

questions.question_text: The relationship between planning and controlling is that:
options: Planning sets standards and controlling measures performance against them

questions.question_text: Planning and controlling are called "inseparable twins" because:
options: Planning gives standards for control, and control gives data for future planning

questions.question_text: A limitation of controlling is that it:
options: May be costly and difficult to apply to qualitative standards

questions.question_text: Resistance to control can be overcome by:
options: Involving employees, explaining the purpose and using fair standards

questions.question_text: The first step in the controlling process is:
questions.explanation: Then measure, compare, analyse and correct.

options: Criteria against which actual performance is measured; they are set on the basis of past performance, benchmarks and plans
questions.explanation: They should be clear and achievable.

questions.question_text: Quantitative standards can be _____, and qualitative standards _____:
options: Measured in numbers; are hard to measure (e.g., customer satisfaction)
Key areas where deviations would most seriously affect results, e.g., cost of raw materials
The areas in which an organisation must perform well to survive and succeed
Personal observation, reports, sample checks and statistical data
The permissible variation from the standard that need not be corrected
Finding the extent and causes of deviations from standards
That the manager can correct, while uncontrollable ones arise from external factors
Changing standards, retraining staff, improving methods or reorganising
questions.explanation: They bring performance back on track.

options: They prove unrealistic or conditions change

questions.question_text: The role of feedback in controlling is to:
options: Provide information about performance to correct future actions

questions.question_text: An essential of a sound control system is:
options: Suitability, simplicity, economy, flexibility and timeliness

questions.question_text: Suitability and simplicity in control mean that:
options: The control system should fit the activity and be easy to understand
questions.explanation: It must serve the needs of the organisation.

options: The cost of control should be less than its benefits
The system can adapt to changes in plans and environment
Information on deviations is provided quickly so that action can be taken in time

questions.question_text: Objectivity and accuracy in control mean:
options: Standards and measurements should be factual and free of bias
Controlling key areas where deviations matter most

questions.question_text: Management by exception helps control by:
options: Concentrating on significant deviations and leaving routine matters to subordinates
Employees should accept the control system as fair and reasonable
Preventive control that anticipates problems before they occur, e.g., inspecting raw materials
Control exercised while the activity is in progress, e.g., supervision
Control after the activity is completed, e.g., a quality check of finished goods
questions.explanation: It uses results to improve future work.

questions.question_text: Feedforward differs from feedback control in that feedforward acts _____ and feedback acts _____:
options: Before the activity; after the activity

questions.question_text: Strategic controls are for _____, tactical for _____, and operational for _____:
options: Long-term goals of the organisation; departmental goals; daily activities
questions.explanation: They correspond to the levels of management.

options: Prevent problems before they occur, while corrective controls fix them after
Control through rules, regulations, hierarchy and procedures
Control through shared values, culture and norms among employees
Budgets, ratios and audit to monitor financial performance
The process of ensuring products meet specified quality standards
questions.explanation: It uses inspection and statistical methods.

options: Maintaining the optimum level of stock to balance cost and availability
questions.explanation: Techniques include EOQ and ABC analysis.

options: Keeping costs within set limits through standard costing and budgets
Budgetary control, ratio analysis, break-even analysis, PERT/CPM and MIS
Gives first-hand information about performance but is time-consuming
questions.explanation: It is useful at lower levels.

options: Reports presenting data in the form of tables, charts and averages for analysis
Uses budgets as standards to compare actual performance; a benefit is cost control, a limitation is rigidity
Sales, production, cash, capital and master budgets
A budget that adjusts to different levels of activity
Preparing the budget from scratch, justifying every expense for each period
A system that sets pre-determined costs and compares them with actual costs
Actual with standard; favourable variance means actual cost is below standard, adverse means above
questions.explanation: It points to areas needing action.

questions.question_text: Standard cost Rs 10 × 1,000 units; actual cost Rs 11,500. The material variance is:
Standard 500 hours at Rs 20; actual 520 hours at Rs 22. The labour cost variance is:

options: The level of sales at which total revenue equals total cost (no profit, no loss)
questions.explanation: It is used in planning and control.

questions.question_text: The break-even point in units is:
options: Fixed cost ÷ (selling price − variable cost per unit)
questions.explanation: The denominator is the contribution per unit.

questions.question_text: FC Rs 60,000; SP Rs 50; VC Rs 30. The BEP is:
FC Rs 1,20,000; P/V ratio 40%. The BEP in value is:
For a target profit of Rs 20,000 with FC Rs 60,000, SP Rs 50 and VC Rs 30, units needed are:
Actual sales Rs 2,00,000; BEP sales Rs 1,50,000. The margin of safety is:
The margin of safety ratio is:
questions.explanation: In the example above it is 25%.

questions.question_text: SP Rs 50 and VC Rs 30. The P/V ratio is:

options: The analysis of financial statements through ratios such as liquidity, profitability and turnover

questions.question_text: Current assets Rs 3,00,000; current liabilities Rs 1,50,000. The current ratio is:
Current assets 3,00,000; stock 1,00,000; current liabilities 1,50,000. The quick ratio is:
Net profit Rs 60,000; capital employed Rs 5,00,000. The ROI is:

options: Cost of goods sold ÷ average inventory
questions.explanation: It shows how fast stock is sold.
It shows the speed of collection.

A systematic evaluation of the effectiveness of management and its policies
Network techniques for planning and controlling projects
questions.explanation: PERT = Programme Evaluation and Review Technique; CPM = Critical Path Method.

questions.question_text: PERT differs from CPM in that PERT uses:
options: Probabilistic time estimates for new projects, while CPM uses deterministic time for routine projects
The longest path through the network, determining the project duration
questions.explanation: Delays on it delay the project.

options: The amount of time an activity can be delayed without delaying the project

questions.question_text: PERT expected time with a = 4, m = 6, b = 14 is:
PERT expected time with a = 2, m = 5, b = 8 is:

options: A bar chart showing the schedule of activities against time
questions.explanation: It is used to monitor progress.

options: Management Information System that provides timely information for planning and control
Total Quality Management, a system of continuous improvement involving all employees
A data-driven approach to reduce defects to 3.4 per million opportunities
Producing and delivering only what is needed, when it is needed, to minimise inventory
Statistical methods such as sampling and control charts to monitor quality
A tool that measures performance across financial and non-financial perspectives

questions.question_text: The four perspectives of the balanced scorecard are:
options: Financial, customer, internal business process and learning and growth
Comparing one's performance with the best in the industry to find improvements
Assigning accountability for costs and revenues to managers who control them
Key Performance Indicators used to measure progress toward objectives
Objectives and Key Results, a goal-setting framework
questions.explanation: They align goals across the organisation.

questions.question_text: A behavioural implication of control is that:
options: Employees may resist control or manipulate data if it feels unfair
Employees monitoring and correcting their own performance
An evaluation of an organisation's social performance and its impact on society
A graph showing process variation over time with control limits
questions.explanation: It flags processes out of control.

questions.question_text: Timely information is essential for control because:
options: Delays allow deviations to grow and make corrective action ineffective
